correctness.rationale: The Hessian identity is an exact determinant calculation with invertible factor 6^4 modulo 5. The support case split exhausts all geometric Jacobian singularities. Affine quadratic initial forms at both symmetry-orbit representatives have full rank, so all 11 rational points are A1. Quartic cohomology and crepant resolution yield a K3. Two independent exhaustive finite-field enumerations give H(F5)=41 and H(F25)=901. Each rational A1 resolution adds q points, giving Y(F5)=96 and Y(F25)=1176. Weil absolute values and maximal trace of Frobenius squared force all 22 eigenvalues to be ±5, and trace 70 gives multiplicities 18 and 4. The package includes the executed complete checker and explicit mathematical derivation; no infinite claim rests solely on finite examples.

value.rationale: A distinguished exceptional-characteristic degeneration of the Clebsch Hessian is known to be supersingular, but its precise arithmetic is a natural invariant not determined by supersingularity alone. Determining maximality over F25 and the full F5 zeta function fixes all extension-field point counts and the exact Frobenius eigenspace split; this supplies useful specific arithmetic data for the Hessian K3 model. The result is not a cosmetic rewrite of the already-known eleven-node geometry.
